title: Kernel detection for graded degree-zero restriction maps
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be a commutative graded ring and $M=\bigoplus_{z\in\mathbf Z}M_z$ an $S$-module with $S_nM_z\subset M_{n+z}$. Let $F=\{(f,d):d>0, f\in S_d\}$, $R_f=S_{(f)}$, $L_f=S_f$, $N_f=M_f$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Write $f\preceq g$ for a homogeneous relation $g^e=af$ with $e>0$. Suppose submodules $Z_f\subset N_f$ have precisely the equal-degree fractions as carriers [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions]. Suppose maps $\lambda_{f,g}:N_f\to N_g$, $\lambda^S_{f,g}:L_f\to L_g$, $\rho_{f,g}:Z_f\to Z_g$, $\rho^S_{f,g}:R_f\to R_g$ and $U_{f,g}=g^{\deg f}/f^{\deg g}$ are given. Assume $f/1$ is a unit with inverse $a/g^e$, multiplication by $f$ on $N_g$ is bijective, $\lambda$ is the unique $S$-linear extension of $x/1$ with formula $x/f^m\mapsto a^mx/g^{em}$, $\lambda^S$ preserves $S$, $\lambda$ is semilinear over $\lambda^S$, $\rho,\rho^S$ are their restrictions, $\rho$ is semilinear over $\rho^S$, and $\rho^S(U)$ is a unit. Then for every $f\preceq g$, each $x\in Z_f$ with $\rho(x)=0$ is killed by some power of $U$, and each $a\in R_f$ with $\rho^S(a)=0$ is killed by some power of $U$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (label lemma-standard-open) (1)(a),(c),(d),(e),(g),(h) and its proof (the formula $x/f^n\mapsto a^nx/g^{ne}$; 'the statements writing $S_{(g)}$ resp. $M_{(g)}$ as principal localizations of $S_{(f)}$ resp. $M_{(f)}$ are clear from the formulas above'); Algebra Section 00JL (label section-proj) for $M_{(f)}$

proof.text: For an ordinary localized-module element y=b/s killed by an S-linear map T from M_f to M_g which fixes b/1, multiply y by s. The identity s*(b/s)=b/1 and linearity give b/1=0 in M_g. Mathlib LocalizedModule.mk_eq applied against zero_mk yields a power g^n annihilating b. Since d>0, write d=d′+1 and factor g^(d*n)=g^(n*d′)*g^n, so it too annihilates b. Mathlib Localization.mk_pow and LocalizedModule.mk_smul_mk show (g^d/f^j)^n*y=0. This calculation is the proved private helper awayKernelFraction; it works without cancelling in S, including nilpotent denominators.

For x in Z_f with rho(x)=0, the given equality between rho and lambda makes its image under lambda zero in N_g. Apply the ordinary calculation with d=deg f, j=deg g. The given value of U and the scalar action induced by algebraMap identify the resulting annihilator with U^n. Injectivity of the submodule inclusion proves U^n*x=0.

For the ring claim, view lambdaS as an S-linear map from S_f to S_g: its preservation of algebraMap and multiplication prove scalar compatibility. The ring S_f is definitionally its ordinary localized module with M=S. Compatibility of rhoS with lambdaS transfers the zero hypothesis. Apply the same calculation with M=S, then use HomogeneousLocalization.val_mul, val_pow and val_injective to obtain U^n*x=0 in R_f.

proof_origin.place: Shorter ordinary-localization proof of Constructions Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), kernel claims (1)(e),(h): clear the source denominator before applying the target zero criterion. Implemented using Mathlib fraction identities.

theorem gradedModuleAwayKernel
    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → AddSubgroup S) [GradedRing 𝒜]
    (𝓜 : ℤ → AddSubgroup M) (h𝓜 : DirectSum.IsInternal 𝓜)
    (hsmul : ∀ (n : ℕ) (z : ℤ) (a : S) (x : M),
      a ∈ 𝒜 n → x ∈ 𝓜 z → a • x ∈ 𝓜 (n + z)) :
    let F := {p : S × ℕ // 0 < p.2 ∧ p.1 ∈ 𝒜 p.2}
    let R := fun f : F ↦ HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f.val.1
    let L := fun f : F ↦ Localization.Away f.val.1
    let N := fun f : F ↦ LocalizedModule.Away f.val.1 M
    let Rel := fun f g : F ↦ ∃ (e k : ℕ) (a : S),
      0 < e ∧ a ∈ 𝒜 k ∧ g.val.1 ^ e = a * f.val.1
    letI : ∀ f : F, Module (R f) (N f) :=
      fun f ↦ Module.compHom (N f) (algebraMap (R f) (L f))
    ∀ (Z : ∀ f : F, Submodule (R f) (N f)),
      (∀ f : F, (Z f : Set (N f)) = degreeZeroFractions
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝒜 n : Set S)) (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝓜 n : Set M))
        (Submonoid.powers f.val.1)) →
    ∀ (lambda : ∀ (f g : F), Rel f g → N f →ₗ[S] N g)
      (lambdaS : ∀ (f g : F), Rel f g → L f →+* L g)
      (rho : ∀ (f g : F), Rel f g → Z f →+ Z g)
      (rhoS : ∀ (f g : F), Rel f g → R f →+* R g)
      (U : ∀ (f g : F), R f),
      (∀ (f g : F), (U f g).val = Localization.mk (g.val.1 ^ f.val.2)
        (⟨f.val.1 ^ g.val.2, ⟨g.val.2, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f.val.1)) ∧
      (∀ (f g : F) (p : Rel f g),
        IsUnit (algebraMap S (L g) f.val.1) ∧
        Function.Bijective (fun x : N g ↦ f.val.1 • x) ∧
        (∀ (e k : ℕ) (a : S), 0 < e → a ∈ 𝒜 k →
          g.val.1 ^ e = a * f.val.1 →
          algebraMap S (L g) f.val.1 * Localization.mk a
            (⟨g.val.1 ^ e, ⟨e, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers g.val.1) = 1) ∧
        (∀ x : M, lambda f g p (mk x 1) = mk x 1) ∧
        (∀ T : N f →ₗ[S] N g,
          (∀ x : M, T (mk x 1) = mk x 1) → T = lambda f g p) ∧
        (∀ (e k : ℕ) (a : S), 0 < e → a ∈ 𝒜 k →
          g.val.1 ^ e = a * f.val.1 → ∀ (x : M) (m : ℕ),
          lambda f g p (mk x (⟨f.val.1 ^ m, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f.val.1)) =
            mk (a ^ m • x)
              (⟨g.val.1 ^ (e * m), ⟨e * m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers g.val.1)) ∧
        (∀ r : S, lambdaS f g p (algebraMap S (L f) r) = algebraMap S (L g) r) ∧
        (∀ (r : L f) (x : N f),
          lambda f g p (r • x) = lambdaS f g p r • lambda f g p x) ∧
        (∀ x : Z f, (rho f g p x : N g) = lambda f g p (x : N f)) ∧
        (∀ r : R f, (rhoS f g p r).val = lambdaS f g p r.val) ∧
        (∀ (r : R f) (x : Z f), rho f g p (r • x) = rhoS f g p r • rho f g p x) ∧
        IsUnit (rhoS f g p (U f g))) →
    ∀ (f g : F) (p : Rel f g),
      (∀ x : Z f, rho f g p x = 0 → ∃ n : ℕ, (U f g) ^ n • x = 0) ∧
      (∀ x : R f, rhoS f g p x = 0 → ∃ n : ℕ, (U f g) ^ n * x = 0)
